summary: Buffered-sender client retry window causes duplicate function/tool invocations when server ack delayed
description:
Issue summary:
Customer using Redwood SDKs (Python and TypeScript) with a buffered-sender enabled on a private deployment observed duplicated external tool/function invocations after a short network blip.

Impact:
- External payment and audit webhooks were invoked twice for ~3% of requests during a 20-minute window.
- Customer Acme Health observed billing and downstream side-effects; they temporarily disabled automatic tool calls.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) in us-east behind customer edge proxy.
- SDKs: python-sdk v0.9.8 (buffered sender enabled), ts-sdk v1.2.1 (buffered sender equivalent).
- Serving runtime: dedicated pool (gpu-a100) running redwood-1.3.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure SDK buffered sender with batch_window=150ms and enable function/tool auto-invoke.
2) Simulate intermittent 200-500ms TCP drop between client and gateway (eg. iptables drop for 250ms).
3) Send a stream-generating request that triggers a single function/tool call mid-stream.
4) Allow the SDK to perform automatic retry and observe webhook/tool invocation count.
logs:
[2026-03-10T14:02:31Z] python-sdk buffered-sender flushed message id=abc123 seq=12
[2026-03-10T14:02:31Z] gateway received batch id=bat-77 processing
[2026-03-10T14:02:31Z] gateway ack delayed due to transient DB lock (120ms)
[2026-03-10T14:02:31Z] python-sdk retry timer expired, resend message id=abc123 seq=12 (client-side retry)
[2026-03-10T14:02:32Z] serving-runtime delivered tool-call request to webhook payment-service txn=tx-999
[2026-03-10T14:02:32Z] serving-runtime delivered tool-call request to webhook payment-service txn=tx-1000
investigation_notes:
- Initial reproduction with customer network emulation reproduced duplicate tool invocations when ack latency crossed buffered-sender flush window.
- SDKs maintain per-message local dedupe keys but the buffered sender batches multiple logical messages into one envelope; the client-side retry path will resend envelopes when no ack is received within batch_window + jitter.
- Gateway de-duplication is currently keyed on request-id header which is set per-envelope. When envelope boundaries shift due to buffering, identical logical function calls may be split across envelopes with different request-ids leading to server-side inability to dedupe.
- Observed additional factor: webhook confirmation token TTL set to 30s; duplicate calls created distinct downstream transaction IDs, complicating reconciliation.
hypothesis: Race between buffered-sender flush+client retry and server ack that is keyed per-envelope. Root cause likely combination of: 1) buffered sender batching semantics producing variable envelope boundaries, 2) client-side retry triggering a second envelope with a different request-id, and 3) server dedupe relying on envelope-level request-id instead of function-call content hash or idempotency token.
resolution:
Workaround provided to customer: disable buffered-sender or increase batch_window to 1000ms and enable per-call idempotency token propagation (client-generated idempotency_key header) for tool/function calls.
Engineering actions planned: server-side dedupe enhancement to consider function-invocation idempotency token (accept client-provided func_id header) and SDK patch to ensure buffered-envelope retains per-call idempotency metadata when splitting or reconstructing envelopes.
Status: in-progress. Patch branches created: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime#pr/1824 and github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk#pr/579. Expected hotfix rollout to prod us-east by 2026-03-15 behind a canary.

Customer (Acme Health Eng - Priya Sharma) 2026-03-10: Confirmed mitigation reduced duplicates but not acceptable for throughput needs. They requested root cause analysis and safe fix.
SRE (Maya Torres) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with iptables delay and confirmed duplicates. Added gateway logs showing ack lag correlating with duplicates. Opened PR for server dedupe improvement.

SDK Eng (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-11: Noted buffered sender reconstructs envelopes on retry and currently drops per-call idempotency headers. Working on SDK patch to preserve per-call idempotency metadata across batching boundaries.
Support (Jordan Patel) 2026-03-12: Sent customer a recommended temporary config (batch_window=1000ms + client idempotency_key) and scheduled a canary test for 2026-03-14.
